meta.description: Tagging taxonomy for the WCT GLP-1 study. Segment annotations in segment_tags.json draw their theme, subtheme, emotion, and sentiment values from this codebook. Editable and versioned; bump schema_version when tags are added or revised.
changelog: 1.0 — initial themes, emotions, sentiment scale, semantic tags.
1.1 — added subthemes to 10 themes with internal nuance.
1.2 — added subthemes to drug_switching, side_effect_concern, injection_experience, education_need, and weight_loss_history after reviewing participant_10.
1.3 — added a `terms` list to every theme: literal surface phrases tagged from the segment tag drawer, parallel to keyword variants.

1.4 — replaced the emotion vocabulary with the Plutchik model (24 intensity levels + 28 dyads); added `tag_groups` and a `group` field on every theme and semantic tag so the segment tag drawer can nest them.
1.5 — added the `decision_factors` tag group; moved risk_calculation, cost_benefit_reasoning, convenience_tradeoff, and conditional_decision into it as the study's core reasoning moves.
1.6 — folded semantic_tags into theme_tags and removed the semantic dimension; former semantic tags are now themes that keep their group.
notes: A segment may carry a theme with no subtheme (general use) or with one or more subthemes.
A subtheme may only be applied if its parent theme is also applied to the segment.
Flat themes (no subthemes) have no `subthemes` key.
Each theme carries a `terms` list of surface phrases reviewers highlighted as belonging to it; empty until phrases are added from the segment tag drawer.
Themes share one set of `tag_groups`; each carries a `group` id used to organize them in the segment tag drawer.
Emotions follow the Plutchik model: 24 intensity levels (low / medium / high for each of the 8 primary emotions) and 28 dyads (named blends of two primaries).

tag_groups.label: Cost & Access
tag_groups.description: Affordability, insurance, supply, and getting hold of medication.

tag_groups.label: Safety & Risk
tag_groups.description: Side effects, complications, and weighing the risks of treatment.

tag_groups.label: Treatment Experience
tag_groups.description: Living with the medication: staying on it, switching, route, and benefits.

tag_groups.label: Clinical Trial Motivators & Barriers
tag_groups.description: What draws participants to a trial and what gets in the way.

tag_groups.label: Education & Self-Management
tag_groups.description: Learning needs and managing one's own care and behavior.

tag_groups.label: Weight Journey
tag_groups.description: Past weight-loss history and the long arc of the participant's journey.

tag_groups.label: Decision factors
tag_groups.description: Reasoning moves — how a participant weighs a choice: risk, cost vs. benefit, tradeoffs, and conditional logic.

theme_tags.description: Awareness of clinical trials or new drugs in development.
Reasoning about how to obtain or retain access to medication.
Weighing risks, side effects, or trial-design probabilities.
Framing the medication as needed or relied upon long-term.
Reasoning about sustaining weight loss after the active treatment phase.
Trading effort or burden against convenience or accessibility.
Practical obstacles that make trial participation harder.
The participant or their clinician actively pushing to get care.
Actively seeking knowledge, education, or trial information.
Narrative of meaningful health improvement or change.
Explicitly weighing cost against benefit.

emotion_tags.description: Mild joy — calm contentment or ease.
Intense joy — elation or overwhelming delight.
Mild trust — openness or willingness to go along.
Trust — confidence in a person, plan, or treatment.
Intense trust — deep respect, reverence, or gratitude.
Mild fear — unease or wariness about what may come.
Fear — alarm at a perceived threat.
Mild surprise — being momentarily caught off guard.
Intense surprise — astonishment or being stunned.
Mild sadness — wistfulness or low mood.
Intense sadness — deep sorrow or anguish.
Mild anticipation — curiosity or attentiveness toward what's ahead.
Anticipation — looking ahead to or expecting something.
Intense anticipation — keen focus, readiness, or resolve.
